newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate Democrats seek tax cut of $90 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate Democrats seek tax cut of $90 billion.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Wednesday his party's tax relief package would be worth about $90 billion over five years, an amount about half the Republican tax plan.

Daschle, of South Dakota, told reporters the tax cut negotiated this year should not be permitted to increase the deficit. One way to pay for it would be to look at corporate tax breaks and other corporate benefits which could be trimmed, he said.
"We have got to draw a very clear distinction between those who need it (a tax cut) and those who don't," he said.

Democrats have said their tax package, which was released Tuesday, would be in line with the size of President Clinton's proposals. Clinton's plan is expected to be around $100 billion and will be released Feb. 6 as part of his budget.

The Democratic plan includes capital gains tax relief for firms with assets under $100 milion a year, eases other corporate tax rules, provides some estate tax relief, and permits homeowners and farmers to rollover property gains. It gives education tax breaks and credits for health insurance.
Both Republicans and Democrats seek to expand contributions to individual retirement accounts.
The Republican plan, valued at $170-190 billion over five years, has as its key elements a $500 per child tax credit and a reduced capital gains tax.
